# Agent + Code and Tools

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](in-context-tool-control_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Gripper Manipulation Models → Agent Architectures → Agent + Code and Tools

Agents write programs or call tools to specify motion targets, with IK, trajectory generation and controllers executing them. Record runtime programming, context and experience reuse, feedback and recovery, and whether model weights change. Learned perception alone does not make the action executor a learned policy; retain the historical category code and catalog path.

| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.1] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-1"></a> | **GPT-Policy｜Tool calls · In-context learning · Visual feedback**<br>[In-Context Robot Learning with VLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19138v1)<br>Dongzhou Cheng, Taoran Yi et al<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `vlm` `in-context-learning` `tool-use` `video-demonstration` `goal-image` `interaction-history` `execution-feedback` `inverse-kinematics` `real-world` | GPT-Policy organizes demonstration keyframes, optional aligned action records, goal images and interaction history as context for an off-the-shelf VLM with no additional training; the VLM calls tools specifying end-effector poses and gripper commands, a motion execution layer converts these into joint trajectories, and observations and execution results update the context for online adaptation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Studies five context families: human videos, robot videos with actions, goal images, self-interaction history and online human interaction, across cloth/notebook pickup, bottle opening, plug manipulation, arrangement and mobile exploration. YAM, ARX X5 and Morphi Kino dual-arm gripper configurations are documented, without establishing full task coverage on every platform. Each experimental condition has three trials; some model comparisons are individual runs and task progress is not success rate. VLM weights stay fixed and feedback updates context. Interpolation, IK and time parameterization execute motions; they do not establish collision-free or reliable contact control. Inter-arm collisions and execution/outcome-verification failures are reported. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.19138v1) · [Project](https://cheng-haha.github.io/GPT-Policy/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-24 |
| [AM.MAN.GRIP.AGENT.ICL.2] <a id="am-man-grip-agent-icl-2"></a> | **AGP｜Runtime programming · Feedback-driven correction · Experience reuse**<br>[Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12541v3)<br>Mengzhao Jia, Yang Lin, Xixin Zhang, Zhihan Zhang, Xiaobai Liu, Meng Jiang<br>**Tags:** `gripper` `bimanual` `agent-architecture` `runtime-programming` `code-generation` `tool-use` `task-planning` `execution-feedback` `failure-recovery` `experience-reuse` `persistent-memory` `in-context-learning` `training-free` `video-instruction` `goal-image` `inverse-kinematics` `real-world` | AGP uses a fixed-weight general-purpose agent to write perception and action programs during execution from visual observations, robot state and physical feedback, execute and revise motions through robot interfaces, and save scripts and experience for reuse, enabling closed-loop manipulation without task-specific training.<br>**Evaluation scope:** A preparation agent organizes video/image/language references and interface documentation; the execution agent requests observations, programs geometric estimates and motion targets, and revises actions. Interfaces accept end-effector poses, joint targets and gripper commands; an independent layer handles Mink IK, trajectories and motor feedback. Experience files update context, not weights. Main hardware uses six-joint YAM arms with parallel grippers, including dual-arm folding. Eight configurations cover four-pair assembly, three block structures, dice flipping, throwing and two folding variants. With GPT-6 Astra, seven score at least 80%; simultaneous folding is 3/5. Each has 5 or 10 trials from predefined scenes under time/request budgets. Mean times span 17.71–50.8 minutes, success-only except throwing's all-session accounting, not real-time action generation. P7 + RealHand L6 bottle lifting is qualitative cross-embodiment evidence only. Official resources include code, videos, step observations, joint trajectories and agent traces, not learned action-policy weights. | arXiv v3 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.12541v3) · [Project](https://agent-as-policy-2026.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/agent-as-policy-2026/agent-as-policy) · [Data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Agent-as-Policy/agent-as-policy) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |
